html:
Activity dependencies and branch execution

An Activity graph is a set of concrete, already-declared operations and prerequisite edges inside one native run. It lets the runtime start a dependent operation as soon as its prerequisites are satisfied, without asking the model to approve each transition. The top-level task queue has a separate dependency owner; see conversation task coordination.

The model supplies tools, known arguments and intended dependencies. The runtime supplies Activity/operation identities, captures targets and authority, validates the graph and applies execution policy. A graph does not grant a capability, reserve resources in advance or provide a syntax for values that a future node has not produced yet.

Accepting a graph

flowchart TD Proposal[Complete model response proposing schedule_activities] --> Structure[Validate graph schema and enabled policy] Structure --> IDs[Check unique node aliases and child call IDs] IDs --> Refs[Validate existing receipt references and declared edges] Refs --> Bounds[Check cycles, connected-component size and run limits] Bounds --> Bind[Capture tools, target authority and concrete effects] Bind --> Accept[Publish graph nodes through decision acceptance] Accept --> Edges[Record predecessor and dependent identities] Structure -->|Invalid| Reject[Reject the affected proposal before accepting nodes] IDs -->|Invalid| Reject Refs -->|Invalid| Reject Bounds -->|Invalid| Reject Bind -->|Invalid| Reject Edges --> Drive[Drive declared ready branches]

dependency_graph.validate_batch checks structure even when the ordinary strict argument-validation guard is relaxed. It rejects cycles, self-dependencies, unknown predecessors, reused node aliases and conflicting child call identities. A connected component includes appended nodes; both the component limit and the size of one new acceptance are checked. The run limit counts retained accepted work, rather than only currently running children.

Dependencies may name nodes in the same proposal or Activities already accepted in this run. New decisions can append nodes; they cannot redefine previous ones. Each node needs an advertised capability, with the explicit ask_user graph exception. Nested orchestration, finish and run-wait tools do not become ordinary graph nodes. Activity normalization and preflight remain owned by activities.py.

The dependency policy validates limits and selects the accepted scope. Missing legacy graph policy is disabled. Current product defaults, existing run snapshots and explicit request selection are different inputs; resumption retains the accepted snapshot rather than silently selecting new defaults.

Driving independent branches

The following illustrates accepted edges B → C and A,C → D. All four operations have known arguments. A and B may overlap within applicable limits; C can start after B while A still runs. D requires both predecessors. These transitions use ordinary Activity workers and do not add a model decision between nodes.

sequenceDiagram participant G as Graph driver participant S as Shared resource scheduler participant A as Activity A participant B as Activity B participant C as Activity C participant D as Activity D G->>S: Admit ready A and B within available worker/capacity limits S-->>G: Accepted reservations par A remains active G->>A: Claim and execute with captured authority and B completes first G->>B: Claim and execute B-->>G: Receipt and completed predecessor state G->>S: Check C after B and current resource constraints S-->>G: C may proceed G->>C: Claim and execute without a model call C-->>G: Receipt and completed predecessor state end A-->>G: Receipt and completed predecessor state G->>S: Check D after A and C S-->>G: D may proceed G->>D: Claim and execute D-->>G: Receipt and final branch state G->>G: Join batch and project updates for ordinary progression

drive first reconciles retained job evidence, then examines current-run pending nodes. A failed prerequisite blocks its dependents while unrelated candidates remain eligible. By default only completed satisfies an edge. If successful dependencies are explicitly not required, a confirmed failed predecessor also qualifies; cancellation, denied execution and unknown outcomes remain unsatisfied.

Ready nodes still pass unknown-effect guards, foreground/dependency worker limits, the per-target Activity limit, the tool budget and atomic resource admission. Existing background work and in-flight futures count toward live Activity limits. A blocked candidate does not occupy an execution future. Resource diagnostics distinguish effect guards, capacity and concrete lock waits.

The driver captures the scheduler wake version before checking work, and completion callbacks notify it. This avoids losing a release that happens before it enters the wait. Pause stops new admissions, preserves completed prerequisites and leaves pending nodes available for an authorized resume. A tool-budget pause also preserves that graph.

Human input is a graph checkpoint

An ask_user node can block its dependents while independent declared branches continue. The parent retains the exact selected question and reply identity. It does not make more model decisions while that question is unanswered. This also works when background promotion is disabled.

sequenceDiagram participant G as Owned graph continuation participant Q as Input Activity participant I as Independent Activity participant U as Existing human-input owner participant S as Native store participant D as Dependent Activity G->>Q: Execute declared ask_user control Q->>S: Save Activity-local question and parent checkpoint G->>I: Admit independent already-declared work I->>S: Retain its actual execution receipt Note over G,D: Dependent work remains pending and model inference is suspended U->>S: Accept answer for the selected Activity and attempt G->>S: Consume answer once through background.resume_inputs G->>G: Re-evaluate predecessor state and ordinary admission G->>D: Execute eligible dependent with its already-known arguments D->>S: Retain receipt G->>G: Select next unresolved human wait or continue

An answer does not rewrite a dependent node's arguments. When the model must interpret the answer or a new result to choose those arguments, it must make an ordinary later decision and append the resulting operation then. OAuth and approvals use their retained continuation owners; jobs and input resumption explains those separate paths.

At completion, required human waits outrank live jobs. Live required work registers a wait; pending branches blocked on unresolved resources retain an explicit blocked result. Graph rendering or a model statement that work is finished cannot override these gates.

Exact inputs come from existing receipts

A dependency edge orders operations; an input binding reads a value. Node names and Activity IDs are not receipt aliases. The graph API rejects a binding to a new node or unfinished Activity structurally, even when strict admission settings are relaxed.

sequenceDiagram participant P as Earlier producer participant S as Scoped receipt store participant G as Graph validation and preflight participant C as Ready consumer participant E as Execution engine P->>S: Commit exact result with operation identity G->>S: Validate existing source receipt and accepted quality checks Note over G,C: Keep binding specification in the Activity, not copied payload values G->>C: Accept consumer and its prerequisite edges C->>C: Wait for dependencies and admission if necessary C->>E: Revalidate before actual execution E->>S: Read authoritative scoped receipt again S-->>E: Scoped receipt or lookup failure E->>E: Apply accepted quality checks and JSON Pointer alt Receipt remains usable E->>E: Bind exact typed value and perform ordinary authorization/dispatch else Source is inaccessible, invalid or no longer acceptable E-->>C: Rejection without executing the bound operation end

execution/bindings.py combines the compact historical/current indexes with current records taking precedence, then reads the authoritative store. Pointer resolution preserves JSON types and original strings. Accepted receipt-quality guards do not bypass run/conversation access checks. Admission or approval waits cannot turn a previous preflight result into permanently cached permission to read a source.

The authoritative details, paging rules and current receipt-read limitations remain in exact results and JSON Pointer. A graph consumer needing a future value must be submitted after that producer has a usable receipt.

Restart and Stop preserve effect history

flowchart TD Recover[Recover current-run graph node] --> State{Interrupted starting or running node?} State -->|No| Keep[Keep retained terminal or pending state] State -->|Yes| Unclaimed{Starting with no invocation claim?} Unclaimed -->|Yes| Pending[Return to pending dependency checks] Unclaimed -->|No| Job{Owned managed job exists?} Job -->|Yes| Observe[Reconnect to same job through background reconciliation] Job -->|No| Receipt{Exact retained result available?} Receipt -->|Yes| Restore[Restore receipt-defined outcome] Receipt -->|No| Unknown[Retain unknown outcome and replay protection] Observe --> Drive[Re-evaluate declared graph with current control fences] Restore --> Drive Pending --> Drive Unknown --> Guard[Block affected dependents or resources under accepted policy]

recover reuses the background Activity recovery owner for claimed synchronous work and managed jobs. It temporarily removes the foreground-batch projection so that projection cannot hide an interrupted node. The owning request path still supplies run ownership and cancellation checks before graph execution.

Task Stop terminalizes unstarted or input-blocked intentions while preserving any actual receipt already retained for active work. A claimed operation without a usable result stays unknown; Stop does not assert process death. Resource release remains with the physical settlement owner, as described in scheduling and release.

Graph updates are bounded projections of retained node state and results. They become reported only when decision acceptance consumes them. Critical-path and overlap metrics come from recorded timestamps; they are neither execution authority nor hardware telemetry.
